content: In Australia, the primary organization responsible for blood donation is the Australian Red Cross Blood Service. In Canada, blood donation services are managed by Canadian Blood Services. Additionally, Héma-Québec operates as an independent, provincial organization separate from Canadian Blood Services. In India, several organizations facilitate blood donation. These include Indian Blood Services, Indian Blood Donors (an independent online blood bank), Friends2Support (another independent online blood bank), and the Marumalarchi Blood Donors Club, which is organized by Vaiko, a politician from Tamil Nadu. In New Zealand, blood donation is overseen by the New Zealand Blood Service, which also maintains an external website for public access to information. In Pakistan, notable blood donation organizations include the Hussaini Blood Bank in Karachi and the Fatmid Foundation, also based in Karachi. In South Africa, blood donation services are provided by the South African National Blood Service (SANBS) and the Western Province Blood Transfusion Service. In the United Kingdom, blood donation is coordinated by several organizations. These include the United Kingdom National Blood Service, which operates a website for England and North Wales, the Welsh Blood Service (Gwasanaeth Gwaed Cymru) for South Wales, and the Scottish National Blood Transfusion Service. In the United States, there is a wide network of blood donation organizations. These include: America's Blood Centers, the largest network of non-profit community blood centers in North America. Blood Centers of the Pacific. The American Red Cross (ARC), which also operates a subsidiary called Give Life. Blood Assurance, based in Chattanooga, Tennessee. The Blood Bank of Hawaii, located in Honolulu, Hawaii. BloodSource, based in Sacramento, California. Carter BloodCare, serving the Dallas-Fort Worth area in Texas. The Community Blood Bank of Northwest Pennsylvania and Western New York. The Community Blood Center of the Ozarks, located in Springfield, Missouri. Community Blood Services, based in New Jersey. The Dayton Community Blood Center, located in Dayton, Ohio. Florida Blood Services, based in St. Petersburg, Florida. Florida's Blood Centers, located in Orlando, Florida. HemaCare, a blood donation organization. The Indiana Blood Center, based in Indianapolis, Indiana. The JMH Blood Bank, located in Abingdon, Virginia, which serves the blood needs of Southwest Virginia. LifeShare Community Blood Services, which serves Northeast Ohio. The Medic Regional Blood Center, serving East Tennessee and Southeast Kentucky. Memorial Blood Centers, based in St. Paul, Minnesota. The New York Blood Center. The Piedmont Blood Center, located in Spartanburg, South Carolina. The Puget Sound Blood Center, serving the Greater Seattle area. The Rhode Island Blood Center, based in Providence, Rhode Island. The South Texas Blood & Tissue Center, located in San Antonio, Texas. The Blood Center, based in New Orleans, Louisiana. The Blood Center of New Jersey, located in East Orange, New Jersey. The Blood Connection, based in Piedmont, South Carolina. United Blood Services, a national blood donation organization. In other countries, the following organizations manage blood donation services: The Etablissement Français du Sang, which is the French National Blood Service. The Irish Blood Transfusion Service in Ireland. The Hong Kong Red Cross Blood Transfusion Service. The Centre for Transfusion Medicine, which is part of Singapore's Health Sciences Authority. The Blood Service of the Finnish Red Cross (Suomen Punaisen Ristin Veripalvelu) in Finland. The Taiwan Blood Services Foundation in Taiwan. The New Zealand Blood Service, which also operates in New Zealand.
